calls.head: Strength in numbers for the Penguins
calls.body: The Penguins roll four lines, but the Sabres lean on their top six. Pittsburgh is one of the league’s best for depth, and Buffalo is one of the worst. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Penguins.
calls.call: The Penguins spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Sabres.

calls.head: The Penguins’ edge in shots from in close
calls.body: The Penguins are the league’s best for shots from in close, and the Sabres are around the middle. That’s the biggest gap between these two, and it isn’t a big one. Shots from in close tend to be the more dangerous ones.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Malkin has a goal and an assist as the Penguins take down the Sabres
paras: It was a busy first period. Jiří Kulich opened the scoring for the Sabres just 31 seconds into the game, his fourth straight game with a goal. Ben Kindel made it 1-1 for Pittsburgh early in the first, and Rasmus Dahlin restored the Sabres’ lead on the power play less than two minutes later. Kris Letang tied it up for Pittsburgh with 40 seconds left in the period. The second period was a wild one. Rutger McGroarty and Blake Lizotte scored less than three minutes apart early in the period to put the Penguins up 4-2. Buffalo pulled Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen after four goals and turned to Alex Lyon for the rest of the second. Josh Norris pulled the Sabres within one midway through the second, but that was as close as they got. Ville Koivunen made it 5-3 for the Penguins late in the period, and Evgeni Malkin added an empty-net goal with just over two minutes left to make it 6-3.

The Penguins outshot the Sabres 28-23, but the Sabres’ chances were the better ones. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Sabres win about six in ten. Sergei Murashov made 20 saves for the Pens. The Penguins improved to 8-15-2, still last in the Metropolitan, while the Sabres dropped to 11-11-4, sixth in the Atlantic.
